items.title: 9.8.4 Salts of weak acids and weak bases

blocks.text: For salts derived from weak acids and weak bases, such as ammonium acetate, NH4CH3COO, both the conjugate acid (NH4+) and the conjugate base (CH3COO-) affect the pH. NH4CH3COO(aq) gives NH4+(aq) + CH3COO-(aq); NH4+ hydrolyses to produce H3O+, NH4+ + H2O gives NH3 + H3O+, and CH3COO- hydrolyses to produce OH-, CH3COO- + H2O gives CH3COOH + OH-. The resultant pH depends on the relative strengths of the conjugate acid and conjugate base: the solution may be acidic, basic or nearly neutral, depending on which reaction is more dominant.

blocks.prompt: Will an aqueous solution of ammonium oxalate be acidic or basic? Explain with equations (Quick Check 9.5c).
blocks.explanation: Ammonium oxalate, (NH4)2C2O4, is the salt of the weak base NH3 and the weak acid oxalic acid, so both ions hydrolyse: NH4+ + H2O gives NH3 + H3O+ and C2O4 2- + H2O gives HC2O4- + OH-. The pH depends on which is stronger; oxalic acid is a considerably stronger acid than ammonia is a base, so its oxalate ion hydrolyses less than ammonium does and the solution is expected to be slightly acidic.

items: Weak acid + weak base salt (NH4CH3COO): both ions hydrolyse, NH4+ giving H3O+ and CH3COO- giving OH-; the pH depends on the relative strengths of the conjugate acid and base.
